articles.title: US will soon announce root cause behind FAA nationwide ground stop
articles.summary:
The US government will announce soon the root cause of the router outage that led to the third-ever nationwide ground stop issued by the US Federal Aviation Administration. But questions remain about whether the FAA's effort to modernize the national airspace system is being done with all the proper risk assessments and adequate agency oversight of the private contractors involved.

The nationwide ground stop blocked flight departures and impacted more than 1 million passengers across the United States for more than four hours on Friday, November 13. More than 12,000 flights were canceled on that day alone, with the number rising to more than 20,000 over the weekend as stranded travelers scrambled to find accommodations or alternative transportation. Some international flights were allowed to depart prior to the broader resumption of air traffic.

Nearly one week later, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told news reporters that government investigators are “very close” to figuring out the root cause of the nationwide ground stop, according to CNN. Bedford also said that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy plans to announce the findings at a news conference as soon as Friday, November 20.

articles.title: Rocket Report: A weekend of ups and downs; Stoke celebrates engine milestone
articles.summary:
Welcome to Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report! Last weekend was a picture of the US launch business in miniature, and emblematic of the opposing trajectories of two of the nation's most experienced rocket makers. First, on Saturday, SpaceX completed a perfect midair catch of its Starship upper stage at its launch pad in Texas after spending nearly a day in orbit. The Super Heavy booster was lost at sea, but SpaceX proved it can recover that piece of the rocket on previous flights. While SpaceX showed it is well on the way to fielding a fully reusable rocket, United Launch Alliance suffered its first-ever total launch failure with the Vulcan rocket. That is terrible news for not only ULA, but also the US Space Force and Amazon, which have booked some 70 launches on Vulcan over the next few years. Your faithful correspondents will take a break from the Rocket Report next week for the Thanksgiving holiday, so we'll see you again the first week of December.

As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.

Europe's leading satellite startup eyes Italian rocket maker. Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company, Ars reports. Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. ICEYE is, by far, the most successful space startup in Europe, with a valuation of more than $12 billion after the company's most recent fundraising round in June.

This Florida case adds to an already complex subplot involving Indigenous tribes, some of which are challenging prediction markets, while others are trying to get in on the action themselves.

In the new lawsuit, the Seminole Tribe contends that two of DraftKings’ current online offerings—the fantasy sports-style “Pick6” and the “Super App” sportsbook—are “illegal" in Florida.

articles.title: Mandarin Oriental is reborn, 12 years and a pandemic later
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – When the last guests checked out of the Mandarin Oriental in September 2014, the hotel promised to be back in six years. 

Makati would have to wait twice as long – with a pandemic in between that set back its original 2020 opening date – but the day has finally arrived.

On Thursday, November 26, Ayala Land opens the new Mandarin Oriental at Ayala Triangle, making good on a promise made more than a decade ago.

The original Mandarin opened on Makati Avenue in 1976, just in time for the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. Designed by National Artist for Architecture Leandro Locsin, it was among the first Mandarin Oriental hotels outside Hong Kong, arriving at a time when Makati was not yet the skyscraper-lined business district it is today.

That iconic structure has since been demolished, and in its place rises Park Central Towers, another Ayala Land development, billed as an ultra-luxury residential twin tower. (READ: Luxury condo resilience: Half of Ayala’s Laurean buyers staying despite pause)

Still, its successor, built just across the street, keeps a connection to the old Mandarin. American architectural firm Skidmore, Owings & Merrill designed the new hotel in collaboration with Leandro V. Locsin Partners, the practice founded by the late architect. 

REINVENTION. The 275-room Mandarin Hotel in Ayala Triangle, Makati City is owned by Ayala Land Hospitality and managed by Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group. Ayala Land handout

The new Mandarin is considerably smaller, at 275 rooms compared with its predecessor’s 413. That was part of the plan from the beginning, when Ayala Land first announced the project in June 2014.

The return of the Mandarin is also part of Ayala Land’s continuing reinvention of Ayala Triangle. Once part of Nielson Airport, the property went on to first house the Makati Stock Exchange and has today evolved into a hub anchored by Ayala Triangle Gardens Towers, with upscale restaurants and landscaped gardens – and finally, a luxury hotel to round it all out.

With the Mandarin, Ayala Land is also making a wager on the Philippines’ place in Asia’s luxury tourism market. The company believes Filipino culture and creativity can be a selling point in their own right, rather than looking to Singapore, Hong Kong, or Bangkok for a blueprint.

Filipino art, craftsmanship, and design feature prominently throughout the property. Ayala Land said it was designed around the idea that “the Philippines need not imitate other luxury destinations to compete with them.”

In the first nine months of 2026, Ayala Land’s leasing and hospitality revenues grew 8% year-on-year to P37.8 billion. Recurring-income businesses also now account for a greater part of the company’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), standing at 55% and up from 44% in the same period last year. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Philippines’ biggest HiFi exhibit set this weekend
articles.summary:
(This is a press release from the November HiFi Show organizers.)

A team of Filipino audio experts is holding a HiFi show this weekend in Makati City. 

The November HiFi Show is the Philippines’ biggest hi-fi exhibition, the country’s premier gathering for music lovers and audio enthusiasts that has been around for 24 years. 

Each year, it brings together leading and local international brands showcasing the finest in high-fidelity and high-quality sound systems, speakers, amplifiers, turntables, and more. 

Beyond the gear, it’s also a treasure trove for collectors, with rare finds, vinyl records, and CDs waiting to be discovered. More than just an exhibition, the November HiFi Show is a celebration of sound culture — where innovation, passion, and community converge. 

“Since 2008, my team of Filipino audio experts and I have been doing this purely for the love of the hobby—no commercial agenda, just a shared mission to build world-class, 100% Filipino-made DIY high-end audio gear,” said veteran business journalist and Rappler columnist Val Villanueva.

The November HiFi Show 2026 will be held on November 28 to 29 at the Makati Diamond Residences, 118 Legazpi Street, Legazpi Village, Makati City. 

Parking can be found nearby Greenbelt Malls, and street side parking is available in Legazpi Village. 

Admission is free for all audio and music lovers, and there’s no need to pre-register. Just walk in and enjoy what the November HiFi Show has to offer. 

Whether you’re a seasoned audiophile or just curious about great sound, swing by Room 802. Let’s talk gear, swap stories, and enjoy the music. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Pope Leo calls COP31 failure ‘troubling,’ urges action on climate change
articles.summary:
VATICAN CITY – Pope Leo XIV on Wednesday, November 25, sharply criticized the failure of UN climate talks over the weekend, calling the outcome “troubling” and urging world leaders to step up efforts to combat climate change.

“In the face of the growing frequency of extreme environmental events linked to the climate crisis, it is troubling that COP31 ended without the international community adopting clear commitments to address it seriously and responsibly,” the pope told pilgrims at his weekly audience in St. Peter’s Square.

“This situation calls for a renewed sense of shared responsibility, new forms of solidarity among nations and fundamental changes in behaviors, socio-economic systems, and the governance of our societies,” said the Pope.

The COP31 talks collapsed on Sunday, November 22, as the European Union and others rejected a final deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkey and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.

The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted was after a summit in Copenhagen in 2009.

Leo is known for speaking carefully in public and makes appeals to the international community in his weekly audiences on a less frequent basis than his predecessor, Pope Francis.

Leo, the first US-born pope, has urged the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics to protect the Earth. Last year, he approved a new Catholic rite of Mass that exhorts people to care for creation, in a first for the global Church. – Rappler.com

articles.title: More connected but lonelier than ever: How do we navigate an AI-reliant world?
articles.summary:
Childhood looks different for many kids nowadays in the age of artificial intelligence and social media. 

Toys are no longer the only things keeping them busy. Screens dominate their free time. And when they want to play with their friends, they don’t always just head outside anymore; they log onto gaming platforms instead. 

And when they become lonely and need someone to open up to, it’s no longer a human hearing them out — but an AI chatbot. For mental health advocates like actress and She Talks Asia co-founder Iza Calzado, the rise of these tools is alarming. Under the guise of connection and offering safe spaces, AI chatbots often just work to normalize isolation, and it’s a reality that many humans who have fallen for the trap have to face. 

“It’s safer to chat with a bot in this landscape. It agrees with you all the time. It does not judge you. It’s never disappointed when you say something. So imagine a child, who perhaps does not feel as confident or as safe in their own home, is lonely, starts talking to a bot, and then eventually becomes friends with a bot,” Calzado illustrated during a panel discussion at Rappler’s 2026 Social Good Summit last Saturday, November 21.  

“Because you know what? This friend will not unfriend me, will not spread rumors about me in school, and will not bully me. That’s how it begins, and that to me is very concerning.” 

Even among adults, AI chatbots have become pseudo-therapists who help rationalize their thoughts, make sense of whatever they’re going through, and validate their feelings — even when they may be in the wrong. The chatbot pulls you in by making you feel seen, and before you know it, you’ve been completely hooked. 

But why does it do this? 

For Empath CEO and founder Steph Naval, it’s simple: AI chatbots are there to make money. 

Steph Naval at We the Humans, Social Good Summit at BGC, Taguig City, on November 20, 2026.

“Chatbots, when you go there for a replacement of therapy or well-being, what happens is that you don’t get the benefit of having difficult conversations and corrective behavior. Because that’s something that you do in therapy,” Naval said, adding that it was in her painful therapy sessions that she was actually able to heal and grow most. 

Must Read

Unpacking mental health chats with AI: Finding comfort, but not treatment

It’s the same with social media, which has become a fierce breeding ground for insecurity. Naval said these apps can detect that through your images and videos, and “responds by pushing certain products or content that can exacerbate these negative thoughts.

“For example, it takes a lot of photos of your body or the gym and then they can detect if you feel insecure. Then they’ll push products to you. So I find that’s something to definitely take note of because that has really caused and affected a generation,” said Naval. 

When technology comes before policy

Social media and chatbots, however, don’t just offer you a false sense of companionship and feed on your biggest vulnerabilities. They have also doubled a platform for groups to promote violence among young children — and this is something that has become apparent in the alarming rise of school shooting incidents in the Philippines. 

Must Read

[Be The Good] Not another school shooting please

Still, Akbayan Representative Perci Cendaña believes that the growing reliance on these chatbots isn’t something you can blame on those who turn to it, especially in countries like the Philippines where mental health services are scarce. From then on, it only leads to a bigger set of issues that the country is not yet equipped to properly address. 

“We lack mental health assistance, that’s why our countrymen go online instead. They rely on chatbots. They rely on the warmth and affirmation they get from these platforms, and this phenomenon, combined with other social realities, are fueling these isolated incidents,” Cendaña said in a mix of Filipino and English. 

“Nauuna ang teknolohiya sa polisiya. Nauuna ang teknolohiya sa government framework (Technology is prioritized over policy. Technology is ahead of the government framework),” he added. 

Perci Cendaña at We the Humans, Social Good Summit at BGC, Taguig City, on November 20, 2026.

This is what Cendaña hopes to address through the National AI Governance Act — which is anchored on human-centeredness. It contains the AI Bill of Rights, which holds that humans should have the authority to override platform systems. 

Cendaña then believes that tech executives and government officials shouldn’t be the only ones making decisions about AI governance. Because it’s human well-being at the very core of it all, civil society should have a seat at the table, too. 

Back to your community

The solutions to the impact of AI and technology on community mental health requires an intensive systemic approach. But these policies are not what we should only rely on, because these safeguards should start at home. 

“Home should be the safest space. That’s the first line of defense — families, friends… So let’s make sure that we are that for our children,” Calzado said. 

Iza Calzado at We the Humans, Social Good Summit at BGC, Taguig City, on November 20, 2026.

Parents need their own community, too, however. It takes more than a village to raise a child in this era, and parents also need their own kind of support and human connection so they can come home strong to their kids. 

For Naval, one of the best ways to do that is to dedicate time to activities that will allow you to interact with other human beings. Take a wellness class. Join clubs for your hobbies. Make the effort to see your friends in person. 

Technology and AI are here to stay. Decentering it, then, requires us to go back to our roots as humans and hone in on that. – Rappler.com

articles.title: FACT CHECK: ICC chamber order on ‘Incident 57’ doesn’t mean Duterte will be released
articles.summary:
Claim: Former president Rodrigo Duterte is set to be released after the International Criminal Court (ICC) dropped one drug-related killing, “Incident 57,” from his crimes against humanity case. 

Rating: FALSE 

Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel bearing the claim has already received 823,000 views, 12,500 reactions, 1,400 shares, and 1,200 comments as of writing. It was posted on November 17 and continues to gain traction up to this date. 

The video shows a photo of Vice President Sara Duterte and her father, who is currently detained at the ICC facility in The Hague, Netherlands. The text on the photo reads, “Tuluyan nang ibinasura ng ICC ang Incident 57 drug war charges laban kay PRRD dahil sa sablay ng petsa.”

(The ICC has definitively dismissed the ‘Incident 57’ drug war charges against [former president Rodrigo Roa Duterte] due to an error in the date.)

Additional text overlaid on the reel claimed that the ICC junked the case and that the Vice President has urged their supporters to pray for her father’s safety upon his supposed return. 

The facts: While the ICC Trial Chamber III’s order to drop “Incident 57” from the list of incidents in the second count of charges against Duterte is genuine, it is not true that he is set to be released following this directive. 

Duterte remains detained in ICC custody. There are no credible news reports or official announcements saying that Duterte can now return to the Philippines or that his case has been dismissed.

In an October 9 ruling, the ICC Trial Chamber III ordered prosecutors to remove Incident 57, a single alleged drug-related killing involving a “high-value target,” because it fell outside the confirmed timeframe of the second charge against Duterte. 

The prosecution then complied with the order. In a document dated October 20, the prosecution said that all references to Incident 57 are now removed from the trial brief and replaced with redacted information.

Duterte is currently facing three counts of crimes against humanity, including murders in and around Davao City allegedly committed by the “Davao Death Squad” while he served as mayor between 2013 and 2016, targeted killings of alleged high-value targets during his presidency between 2016 and 2017, and murders and attempted murders during barangay-level anti-drug operations between 2016 and 2018. 

List of incidents: Aside from Incident 57, which the ICC chamber ordered removed, there are many other active incidents included in the charges against Duterte. In October, the ICC trial chamber approved the addition of seven new incidents to the charges, raising the total number from 49 to 56. 

Duterte was arrested in March 2025 for crimes against humanity. He is set to face trial on November 30.

Previous fact checks: Rappler has fact-checked similar false claims about Duterte’s detention:

FACT CHECK: Post falsely claims ICC junked Duterte case over ‘fabricated’ evidence 

FACT CHECK: Duterte not back in PH; post takes out of context old news report, video 

FACT CHECK: Photos of Duterte being assisted in ICC courtroom are AI-generated

– Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com 

Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024. 

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Senate prioritizes feeding program in push for higher 2027 DepEd budget
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – Senator Bam Aquino recommended making the school-based feeding program the top priority for an additional budget among other Department of Education (DepEd) programs in 2027.

Overall, the Senate finance committee recommended P915.49 billion for the proposed new general appropriations of the DepEd and its attached agencies.

That amount is P4.91 billion higher than the P910.5 billion approved by the House of Representatives, but P1.25 billion lower than the P916.75 billion in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP). 

Among the changes, the Senate panel added P11 billion to the school-based feeding program, pushing the proposed allocation to P22.4 billion.

But Aquino, as the DepEd’s budget sponsor, plans to seek an additional increase for the program. “At the proper time, this representation, alongside some other colleagues, will introduce an amendment to increase the budget for the school-based feeding program by P6,265,478,145,” he said during the plenary deliberations.

That would raise the program’s budget to P28.7 billion, higher than the P25.7 billion in the 2026 national budget.

The additional funding would also expand the universal feeding to cover kindergarten to Grade 2, reaching another 1.8 million students in 2027. This follows the phased implementation under the national children’s nutrition bill, which has been ratified but not yet signed into law. 

The P28.7-billion budget would cover 124 feeding days, or from June to December in 2027, at P30 per meal.

Must Read

After Congress, expanded nutrition program bill’s next test is funding

Aquino remains hopeful that they can still set a higher budget for the education sector.

“I have spoken to the Senate President multiple times to share my frustration with the fiscal space provided for this important agency,” he said in the plenary. 

“We have proposed a much bigger budget only to be met with an answer that we didn’t like, which was that the fiscal space is very limited — which we understand. Mr. [Senate] President, I believe that we can still increase this before the period of amendments,” he added in a mix of English and Filipino.

ARAL Program’s low disbursement

Aquino also supports funding for the Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program in 2027. There is no separate line item for it in the 2027 NEP.

However, in the Senate committee report, the ARAL Program remains unfunded.

“Talo pa tayo ng House. P300 million, nakalagay sila. Tayo, wala,” Senator Joel Villanueva said during his interpellation. (The House outdid us. They allocated P300 million. We did not put anything.)

Villanueva noted that 11 million students have been identified as needing remediation sessions in school year 2026-2027.

Aquino told senators that the ARAL Program still has unspent funds from this year. During the 2026 budget talks, it was the Senate that pushed P8.9 billion for the learning recovery initiative. 

“More than half of the P8.9-billion budget for this year was released very late, only in July and August. Therefore, because of the late release, meron pa pong pondo, ‘yon ang gagamitin (there is still funding, which will be used) next year,” he explained.

He added that the disbursement rate, which refers to actual payments made, is only at 13%. 

According to Aquino, the DepEd is already in the process of disbursing the funds in the next few weeks, with Education Secretary Sonny Angara promising a faster process. Angara was standing beside the senator during the deliberations. 

“We know that it can work. We’ve been talking about our learning gaps for so many months. The main solution to the learning gap is really a remediation program,” Aquino said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Trump did not praise Davao City’s energy security efforts
articles.summary:
Claim: US President Donald Trump praised Davao City for its energy security efforts.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook reel bearing the claim was posted by the page Baste Duterte fan on November 21. The video has received 76,000 views, 1,700 reactions, 517 shares, and 139 comments as of writing. 

The video shows Trump in a bilateral talk with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on November 18.

Text overlaid on the video reads, “[Number one] energy save security Davao City in the world.” The post further claimed that Marcos was supposedly taken aback when he heard Trump mention Davao City, the stronghold of his political rivals, the Dutertes.

Another Facebook reel, which has already garnered an estimated 704,000 views, also claimed that the US government will provide Davao City with a new energy project. 

The facts: Nowhere in Trump’s statements during the bilateral talks did he say that Davao City was number one in the world for its energy security efforts. He also did not mention any new US government energy project for the city. No global rankings or news reports identify Davao City as a top city for energy conservation and security, contrary to the claim.

Reports from news outlets such as GMA News quoted Trump saying, “We have more energy than any country in the world by double.” The misleading post misinterpreted Trump’s pronunciation of “double” as “Davao.”

Trump was actually referring to US energy production. He claimed that the country is now the leading producer of oil and natural gas, surpassing the combined supply of Russia and Saudi Arabia, with the US leader also referencing its “acquisition” of Venezuela’s oil reserves. Trump also said the US aims to increase energy exports to Pacific allies, including the Philippines. 

Trade deal: The posts circulated following Trump’s arrival in Manila on November 17 for a state visit and to participate in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations-US Special Summit, as well as the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue leaders’ summit.

During his visit, the US leader highlighted what he described as the “biggest trade deal” between the Philippines and the United States. The US is strengthening its defense partnership with the Philippines while signaling interest in expanding cooperation on energy security, particularly in nuclear energy. 

US energy production: Trump’s remarks appeared to refer primarily to the United States’ energy production, particularly oil and natural gas. He has previously made the claim that the US is producing more oil and gas “than Russia and Saudi Arabia combined.” According to an article by PolitiFact, this remark is “mostly true,” but added that the US lead over the two countries “is built on the other liquids, not crude oil.”

According to Our World in Data, a project by UK-based nonprofit Global Change Data Lab, when considering total energy supply across different sources, including coal, oil, natural gas, renewables, and nuclear energy, China ranks first globally, with approximately 45,000 terawatt-hours in 2025.

Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar false claims about Trump:

FACT CHECK: Trump did not call an ABS-CBN reporter ‘stupid’ 

FACT CHECK: Trump didn’t issue an arrest warrant against Marcos 

FACT CHECK: No reports of Trump wanting to talk to Dela Rosa 

FACT CHECK: No report of Trump courtesy call on Sara; Marcos remains president 

FACT CHECK: No Trump plan to secure Duterte’s release from ICC 

– Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com 

Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

articles.title: Who is new COA chair Douglas Michael Mallillin?
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Appointments (CA) on Monday, November 23, confirmed Douglas Michael Mallillin as the new chairperson of the Commission on Audit (COA), despite initial objections from Senator Imee Marcos over the agency’s impartiality.

Mallillin, who was appointed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as commissioner in February 2025, will replace former COA chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba who was appointed to the Supreme Court (SC).

Senator Marcos initially moved to defer Mallillin’s confirmation, citing concerns over the COA’s alleged use as an “instrument of political harassment” against members of the opposition.

“For the reason that we require further enlightenment on the vision and mission of the COA that will be effective for accountability in the future, and because the government’s auditing powers should not be wielded selectively against the opposition — the consequences extend far beyond the individual officials immediately affected,” the senator said.

“And the chilling effect threatens the ability of legislators to discharge their constitutional duties without intimidation or political retaliation,” she added.

The senator later withdrew her objection after Mallillin assured the CA that the commission would uphold its constitutional independence.

Under his leadership, Mallillin said he would push for the modernization of government auditing through artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, and paperless systems to strengthen the detection of irregularities in public spending.

“One of the main programs is actually to upskill and to give the necessary capability to our auditors to audit effectively and efficiently,” Mallillin said.

Previous government posts

Mallillin previously served as ad interim COA commissioner and Director IV under the Office of the COA Chairperson.

He also worked as an associate prosecutor at the Department of Justice and deputy commissioner at the National Telecommunications Commission.

Mallillin graduated magna cum laude in accountancy at Saint Louis University in Baguio City. He topped the 1986 Certified Public Accountant Licensure Examination and passed the 1996 Bar Examinations.

In February 2025, the High Court tapped Mallillin to provide expert opinion on the Department of Finance’s (DOF) directive ordering government-owned and controlled corporations, including PhilHealth, to remit excess funds to the National Treasury.

During the oral arguments, justices questioned Mallillin’s explanations, which appeared to align with the DOF’s position on the fund transfer. He was later excused by SC Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier as he “might be charged with partiality or bias” when the case reaches the COA.

In December 2025, the SC ruled that the government must return P60 billion in PhilHealth funds transferred to the National Treasury and permanently prohibited the transfer of the remaining P29.9 billion. The Court also declared the relevant provision of the 2024 General Appropriations Act and DOF Circular No. 003-2024 unconstitutional.

Mallillin was appointed COA commissioner in February 2025 and later confirmed by the CA in June of that year. As COA chairperson, he will serve the unexpired term of Cordoba, which ends on February 2, 2029. – Rappler.com

The appointment followed the succession order stipulated in the university's bylaws and organizational regulations, according to the university. The position has been vacant since late July, when Ko Gi-bok was removed from office over allegations of sexual assault involving a former student. Hahm received his doctorate in political economy from Carnegie Mellon University in the United States. He previously taught at Georgetown University and Korea University before joining Kyonggi University in 2021 as dean of its Graduate School of Political Studies. As acting president, he will oversee the university's academic and administrative affairs until a new president is appointed. articles.title: Lee calls for swift public housing supply to help stabilize market
articles.summary: President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday called for the swift supply of public housing in a bid to stabilize the housing market. The president made the call during a meeting to promote public housing in Seoul's northwestern district of Eunpyeong, stressing the importance of speeding up housing supply and curbing real estate speculation. The remarks came as housing prices in Seoul remain prohibitively high following years of runaway price growth. The president said sluggish construction activity and a decline in construction permits between 2022 and 2025 led to a housing shortage, destabilizing the housing market. "It is important to expand housing supply and provide housing as quickly as possible," he stressed. To this end, the government plans to annually supply 240,000 public housing units through 2030, which he said would mark the highest level of home supplies on record. The president also stressed the importance of improving the quality of public housing, noting that it should serve as a stepping stone for people seeking to buy their own homes.

articles.title: Who is Kang Kum-sil?
articles.summary: President Lee Jae Myung's pick for spy agency chief, former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil, is drawing attention as she is returning to the main venue of politics after a decade out of the political spotlight. If the National Assembly confirms her for the post, Kang would become the first woman to lead the National Intelligence Service since the agency's predecessor was founded in 1961. Kang, 69, became the first justice minister under President Roh Moo-hyun in 2003. At 46, she was the youngest person and the first woman to hold the post. She remained the only woman to serve as justice minister until Choo Mi-ae, now governor of Gyeonggi Province, was appointed in 2020. Born on Jeju Island in 1957, Kang attended Kyunggi Girls’ High School and studied law at Seoul National University, long seen as the classic path into Korea's legal elite. She passed the bar exam in 1981 and served as a judge from 1983 to 1995. Seoul education superintendent Jung Geun-sik sees that possibility, but teachers experimenting with the technology offer a more cautious picture of what it takes to change how students are taught and tested. Speaking at Tuesday’s forum on the future of assessment, Jung recalled his earlier proposal to abolish the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) by 2040. Recent AI developments and high-profile cheating incidents, he said, had led him to question whether the CSAT could even last that long. “At this pace, I wonder whether the CSAT will be viable next year or the year after. I had proposed abolishing it in 14 or 15 years, but the incidents surrounding this year’s exam have left me feeling that its lifespan may be much shorter,” he said. articles.summary: First lady Kim Hea Kyung on Wednesday attended a concert by an orchestra composed of visually impaired musicians, along with this year's college entrance exam takers. The concert, held in Incheon, west of Seoul, featured the Hyegwang Blind Orchestra, a group of around 50 visually impaired musicians, and was intended to encourage high school seniors who took the grueling college entrance exam earlier this month. The first lady attended the concert at the invitation of a student from Hyegwang School, an educational institution for visually impaired students in Incheon, whom she met last month at an event marking the 100th anniversary of the Korean braille system. Kim praised the orchestra's "enthusiasm and efforts" in creating harmony, while commending the high school seniors in attendance and expressing her hope that they would go on to make their mark in the wider world.

articles.title: Lee vows legal revision to punish domestic violence, even without victim's request
articles.summary: President Lee Jae Myung said Wednesday that his government will seek to revise the law to enable punishment for perpetrators of domestic violence even when their victims fail or refuse to file a complaint against them. The president made the remarks in a post on his X account to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, adding that it was the state's duty to create a society where women can live without fear. In Korea, perpetrators of domestic violence can avoid punishment if victims express a wish not to have them punished. articles.title: Population mobility up slightly in October on base effect
articles.summary: The number of Koreans who moved to new residences rose slightly in October from a year earlier due to a low base effect, but the downside trend continued, government data showed Wednesday. Around 453,000 people changed residences to other administrative districts in October, up 2.6 percent, or 11,000, from a year earlier, according to the monthly tally from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The ministry attributed the on-year increase to a base effect as the number fell sharply in October last year amid the Chuseok holiday season. This year's Chuseok fell in September based on the lunar calendar that changes from year to year. However, the ministry said the country's population mobility is in a steady decline from a long-term perspective amid a rapidly aging and decreasing population. The monthly figure dropped to 378,000 people in September, marking the lowest level since 1973. By region, Seoul reported a net outflow of 5,560 people, and the southeastern port city of Busan also recorded a net outflow of 768. articles.title: Births in Korea jump 12.2% in September, fastest 9-month growth on record
articles.summary: The number of babies born in Korea rose 12.2 percent in September from a year earlier, with the cumulative nine-month tally increasing at the fastest pace on record, government data showed Wednesday. A total of 25,113 babies were born in September, up 12.2 percent, or 2,731, from a year earlier, rising for the 27th consecutive month, according to the Ministry of Data and Statistics. It marked the largest figure for any September in eight years, while the year-on-year growth rate was the second highest for the month, following the 16.6 percent rise recorded in 2007. For the first nine months of the year, the number of newborns totaled 218,896, up 14.3 percent from 191,593 a year earlier, marking the sharpest year-on-year growth since the ministry began compiling related data in 1981. The recent increase in births came amid a growing number of marriages, a rise in the population in their 30s and more positive attitudes toward having children. "For us to address this together, partner nations must develop the capacity to solve their own problems and grow," she said. articles.title: Remains of Korean Army corporal killed in Vietnam War to be returned home
articles.summary: The remains of a Korean soldier who died while serving in the Vietnam War will return home, marking the repatriation 59 years after his death, the defense ministry said Wednesday. The ceremony marking the return of late Army Cpl. Ahn Gyu-tae will take place at Seoul Airport in Seongnam, south of Seoul, overseen by Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul, according to the ministry. His remains will be transferred home from Hawaii via the Air Force's C-130 aircraft, it added. Ahn, who served as an Army corporal under the 9th Infantry Division, was deployed to Vietnam in August 1966 in the midst of the war between communist-backed North Vietnam and the United States and its allies, including South Vietnam and Korea. There, he took part in several military operations before he died from a critical gunshot wound that he sustained during a search mission in 1967. He was 23 at the time. articles.title: Father Ham Je-doe, who made more than 60 trips to North Korea, dead at 93
articles.summary: CHEONGJU — Father Ham Je-doe, born Gerard Hammond, an American Maryknoll missionary who spent more than six decades in Korea and devoted himself to humanitarian work in North Korea, died Monday. He was 93. The Diocese of Cheongju announced that Father Hammond, who had been hospitalized at Cheongju St. Mary's Hospital due to age-related illness, died at 7:46 a.m. Monday. Born in Philadelphia in 1933, Hammond graduated from Maryknoll Seminary and was ordained a priest before choosing Korea as his first mission destination in 1960. After arriving in Korea, he served as director of the Sacred Heart Orphanage in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, caring for children. He later spent more than 30 years conducting pastoral work in the Diocese of Cheongju, dedicating himself to evangelization and social service in the region. In particular, while serving as the first pastor of Sudong Catholic Church in Cheongju, he donated an inheritance from his grandparents to secure land for a church and kindergarten. articles.title: Korea slashes nationality reinstatement wait times to 9 months for ethnic Koreans living abroad
articles.summary: The Ministry of Justice has significantly accelerated the nationality reinstatement process for ethnic Koreans living abroad, cutting the average review time by four months — from 13 months down to nine. For applicants experiencing the fastest processing, wait times have been reduced by as much as seven months, offering swift relief to thousands eager to formally reconnect with their homeland. articles.title: As AI cheating fears soar, does college matter that much in Korea?
