articles.title: Jensen Huang is back, but it won’t be business as usual for Taiwan’s tech industry
articles.summary:
Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia was a shot in the arm for the Taiwan stock market, with investors and tech players heaving a sigh of relief.

But observers say it will not be business as usual for Taiwan’s tech industry, as manufacturers will now have to tread carefully around the geopolitics of the AI supply chain.

Huang, a Taiwanese-American, was reinstated as Nvidia’s chief executive on Nov 23, 11 days after he resigned over a scandal linked to an alleged Chinese spy.

Taiwan’s stock market was hit hard. Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai met on Nov 23 executives from tech companies and financial firms to discuss ways to stabilise the stock market, after Taiwanese shares plunged almost 18 per cent, their worst week since 1991.

After news broke that Huang was back, Nvidia shares soared 31.5pc, while Taiwan’s main index TAIEX jumped 9pc.

Hsu Ching Sheng, who owns Nvidia shares, said he was so excited after seeing the late-night news that he could not sleep.

“It’s been a real roller coaster lately – going from initial disbelief… to holding on to the firm belief that (Nvidia shares) would bounce back,” the 26-year-old personal trainer told The Straits Times.

“Jensen Huang’s return is definitely a huge plus for the Taiwan stock market. Everyone knows he’s a staunch supporter of Taiwan’s supply chain… it’s fair to say he’s a major driving force behind the Taiwan stock market.”

Huang’s resignation from Nvidia, the company he co-founded and had run for 33 years, came after he admitted to infidelity. He was linked to Alice Huang, a woman US officials suspect of links to Chinese intelligence.

‘Stand with Jensen’

Calls for the “godfather of AI” to return soon began and a “Stand with Jensen” petition was backed by more than 200,000 signatures, including that of tech tycoon Elon Musk.

Last week, the Taipei 101 skyscraper even lit up with messages such as “Taiwan ​loves Jensen” and “Taiwan AI co-create the future”, organised by prominent figures from Taiwan’s technology industry.

The 63-year-old was reinstated after lobbying from US President Donald Trump, who said he spoke to Nvidia’s board directly to press for Huang’s return.

Chang Ruay-shiung, honorary chair professor of National Taipei University of Business (NTUB), said Huang has played a major role in building Nvidia’s technological advantage, corporate culture and global business relationships.

“Finding someone who can replace him at this stage of the AI race would be extremely difficult,” he told The Straits Times.

Nvidia had issued a press release reaffirming its support for Taiwan’s supply chain, but it would be hard to replace Huang’s personal relationships with Taiwanese suppliers.

The Nvidia CEO has made a habit of publicly thanking his Taiwanese suppliers, and is known for hosting “trillion-dollar dinners” with their bosses, named after the combined market value of the firms at the table.

Lien Hsien-ming, president of Chung-Hua Institute of Economic Research, said that Huang did not encourage aggressive price-cutting among suppliers and did not squeeze their margins.

“We can say that Jensen Huang was friendlier to Taiwan (than other US tech firms),” he said. “He prefers to collaborate to build up the supply chain.”

Saga not over yet

NTUB’s Chang noted that Huang’s return to Nvidia will not be the end of the controversy, as the US’s investigation into the loopholes that allowed advanced Nvidia chips to be routed to China remains unfinished.

While the affair captured headlines, Alice Huang is just one thread of a US probe into a cross-border network of server makers, AI data centres and shell companies that allegedly moved export-banned Nvidia chips into China.

Under US export rules, Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips cannot be shipped to China without a US licence, and re-exporting them from other countries without one is also a violation.

In its Nov 23 statement, the Nvidia board said it has formed a National Security and Export Control Committee made up of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. Nvidia also has a new job opening – a chief compliance officer to oversee compliance across the firm.

Huang, who apparently had 60 executives reporting directly to him, is expected to face more checks and balances going forward.

Taiwan manufacturers and suppliers are also likely to face greater responsibility for identifying the final customers and tracking where their products are used, said analysts.

“Taiwanese companies may consequently face higher compliance costs, longer approval procedures and greater legal risks. But they will benefit from the so-called non-red supply chain,” said Chang, referring to supply chains that exclude Chinese companies.

“In the future, export control compliance will become an important part of the competitiveness of Taiwan’s semiconductor industry.”

Lien of the Chung-Hua Institute of Economic Research said smaller companies that cannot meet compliance costs may be in trouble.

“Now, you have to be very careful. If you are caught, the consequences will be grave. The fines for (violating) national security regulations can be huge,” he said.

NTUB’s Chang said Huang’s return has ended Nvidia’s immediate leadership crisis, but the whole saga has opened a much larger debate about the relationship between technology companies, government power and national security.

“Taiwan, given its central role in the global semiconductor industry, cannot afford to ignore that debate,” he said.

articles.title: Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form Israel's government
articles.summary:
Israel’s Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, said on Tuesday it agreed to sign a coalition pact with a right-wing opposition party as it ​seeks to form a government following last month’s election.

Yashar said that Eisenkot ‌had met with Avigdor Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, earlier on Tuesday and they agreed on a deal afterward, the first such alliance since the election.

Israel’s parliament was sworn in on Nov ​10 without a new government, after the election on Oct 27 stripped Prime ​Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority but left others with no clear ⁠path to power.

President Isaac Herzog has tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, while Netanyahu ​remains caretaker prime minister.

Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but ​still lost its majority. It now holds 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats.

Eisenkot’s centre-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners — including Lieberman — hold just 48 seats.

But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s ​Arab minority, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition ​to Netanyahu.

The agreement between Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Lieberman, whose party won 7, ‌was ⁠something of a surprise, since Lieberman had been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Netanyahu.

Lieberman has also said his main goal is to oust Netanyahu from power.

Eisenkot has until Dec 6 to ​form a government ​under a 28-day mandate, ⁠but he could ask for a 14-day extension.

If he fails, Netanyahu would get a shot. If no one is able to ​form a government, another election will be held next year.

Talks are also ​ongoing between ⁠Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a unity government.

The left-wing Democrats party, which won 8 parliament seats, separately said it was suspending talks with Eisenkot because of progress ⁠in his ​talks with Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible unity government ​and given the deadlock in negotiations to form a ‘change government.’

Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, has said he prefers ​a government without Netanyahu but with Arab parties.

articles.title: In an Egypt village, generations of Palestinians denied a normal life
articles.summary:
Shamma Abu Hussein is possibly the last person in her village of refugees to have lived in historic Palestine.

Living in Egypt, she has watched three generations of her family grow up in legal limbo.

She was among the hundreds of thousands who fled or were expelled during the creation of the State of Israel in 1948, whose descendants number in the millions.

Now she fears that the effects of the Gaza war and rhetoric from Israeli ministers calling for Gazans to be expelled means history is repeating itself.

“After all the suffering they’ve endured,” the 90-year-old said, “they now want to uproot them from their homes.”

“I remember what I went through,” she told AFP from a low-slung brick house in Geziret Fadel, a village tucked among the fields and irrigation canals of Egypt’s Sharqiya province, about an hour northeast of Cairo.

She was recalling her family’s flight from Beersheba, now in southern Israel, where they lived before fleeing the hostilities that accompanied Israel’s creation, which Palestinians remember as the Nakba, or catastrophe.

One evening, as flames lit up the sky, elders rushed the children onto camels and into the desert, where Abu Hussein’s family trudged for days without food or water until reaching Egypt, losing her mother along the way.

The settlement where they eventually found refuge has grown into a community of around 4,000 Palestinians.

Many have spent their entire lives in Egypt, yet they say they face bureaucratic hurdles to access education, healthcare and other public services because they are treated as foreigners rather than citizens.

Generations in limbo

Inside her home, the wiry Abu Hussein sat on a worn sofa, a faded Bedouin tattoo tracing her chin.

Around her, dozens of grandchildren and great-grandchildren crowded the doorway and walls, filling in names and dates blurred by nearly a century of life.

Outside stretched a maze of narrow alleys and unfinished houses, with open sewers running through the village’s dirt lanes.

Residents spoke less about returning to their ancestral home than about education, employment and stability.

“I was born in Egypt. My father was born in Egypt. My children were born in Egypt,” said Selmi Soliman al-Namouli, a 63-year-old agricultural labourer and father of 10.

“But when it comes to paperwork, I am treated as a foreigner.”

Namouli said residency renewals, paid for in US dollars, school fees and other administrative costs placed such a heavy burden on his family that he could not afford to send his bright daughter, Asmaa, to university.

His nephew, Farid Khaled al-Namouli, 25, also gave up on higher education.

“When I reached preparatory school, I started to love education and wanted to continue,” he said. “But I kept running into obstacles with the paperwork.”

He left school and found work in a clothing shop in the village, where many residents never completed their education.

‘Ongoing Nakba’

The Namoulis are far from alone, according to Lubnah Shomali of the Palestinian refugee rights organisation BADIL, who said Palestinians across Egypt face similar challenges.

Researchers estimate that around 50,000 Palestinians displaced by earlier conflicts were living in Egypt before the latest Gaza war. Since the conflict began, more than 100,000 more have arrived.

The UN agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA, counts 3.5 million registered in Jordan, Syria and Lebanon.

The Gaza war has revived fears of another Nakba, but Shomali said Palestinians were already living through one.

“The most apt description of the situation for Palestinians is an ongoing Nakba because the displacement continues,” she told AFP, adding that generations of Palestinians have been trapped in a “coercive environment” that limits access to education, healthcare and other basic rights.

Egyptian officials have repeatedly said that Egypt has provided medical care and education to Palestinian refugees and has opposed any attempt to permanently displace them from their land.

Palestinians in Egypt once enjoyed access to education and employment largely on a par with Egyptian citizens under former president Gamal Abdel Nasser.

But after Egypt’s 1978 peace treaty with Israel and the assassination of culture minister Yusuf Sibai by members of the Palestinian group Abu Nidal, the regulations were tightened.

Right of return

Moreover, unlike in Jordan, Syria and Lebanon, where UNRWA offers schooling, the agency has never operated in Egypt, said Dawn Chatty, an emeritus professor of anthropology and forced migration at the University of Oxford.

“Education is what gave Palestinians hope,” Chatty told AFP.

“It allowed many refugees elsewhere in the region to find work abroad and support their families through remittances. But in Egypt, that did not happen.”

Successive Egyptian governments have also rejected naturalising Palestinians, arguing it could undermine their right of return, a position Shomali disputed.

The Egyptian foreign ministry did not respond to an AFP request for comment.

Despite the life she built in Egypt, Abu Hussein has never abandoned the idea of returning home.

“We had a good life back home,” she said. “If everyone here goes back, I’ll go with them.”

articles.title: Bangladesh garment workers win 36pc wage rise
articles.summary:
Bangladesh’s garment workers won a 36 per cent minimum wage increase on Wednesday, officials said, after weeks of sometimes violent protests causing hundreds of millions of dollars in business losses.

The South Asian nation, the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, has seen widespread demonstrations since October by workers demanding higher pay.

The garment industry, which clothes millions of consumers across Europe and North America, is Bangladesh’s economic lifeline, generating four-fifths of export earnings and employing more than four million people.

After the deal was struck following lengthy negotiations with factory owners, workers’ representatives urged people to return to factories.

“Although we are not completely satisfied, the outcome is not entirely bad either,” Babul Akhter, the labour representative on a wage board set up to resolve the crisis, told reporters.

“Previously, workers used to get a wage revision every five years, but this time they are getting a revised wage after three years.” It was not immediately clear how workers — who clashed with police in industrial zones on Tuesday — would react to the deal.

Workers initially demanded a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($240), up from 12,500 taka.

They say their pay has failed to keep pace with the rising cost of food, housing, transport and health care.

Judge Syed Azad Subhani, the chairman of the government-appointed garment industry wage board, said the “majority supported a minimum wage of 17,000 taka”, after a vote early Wednesday.

The wage hike will take effect in January.

‘Export engine’

Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said on Sunday that protests had cost the industry an estimated $428 million, while orders worth $254m had shifted to other countries.

The disruption came ahead of the busy Christmas season.

The garment industry, which supplies major international brands including Fruit of the Loom and Levi Strauss, earns around $38 billion a year.

Bangladesh supplies more than 150 countries with ready-made garments, according to the BGMEA, which represents around 4,000 factories.

The United States is its biggest individual market, while the European Union is its largest trading bloc.

When Bangladesh won independence from Pakistan in 1971, it was among the world’s poorest countries, with its economy devastated by war.

The expansion of garment production helped transform the nation of around 170 million people from a predominantly agricultural economy into a major global manufacturing hub.

Bangladesh’s central bank calls the garment sector the “country’s export engine”. But its success has been built on a vast relatively low-paid workforce, with longstanding disputes over wages, working conditions and labour rights.

The 2013 Rana Plaza factory collapse, which killed more than 1,100 people and injured thousands, exposed appalling safety conditions in the industry, with workers employed in dangerous buildings and often lacking adequate labour protections.

The disaster prompted major international efforts to improve workplace standards, including an agreement between global clothing brands and trade unions to inspect factories and enforce safety measures.

articles.title: Pakistan calls for human control over decisions on nuclear weapons use
articles.summary:
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has called for keeping decisions on the use of nuclear weapons under human control and warned that artificial intelligence (AI) systems must never be used to target nuclear command, control and communications systems.

The warning was delivered by Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, during a high-level open debate of the UN Security Council on Wednesday on conflict resolution in an era of rapid technological change.

The ambassador’s remarks carry particular significance for South Asia, where both Pakistan and India possess nuclear weapons, making the security of nuclear command, control and communications systems an important regional concern.

“This is most critical in the nuclear domain, where decisions on the use of nuclear weapons must remain under human control, and AI systems must never be used to target nuclear command, control and communications systems,” Ambassador Shah said.

He cautioned that the rapid development and convergence of emerging technologies were adding unprecedented speed, scale and complexity to international security challenges and could intensify the ongoing arms race.

Ambassador Shah said technology itself was neutral, with its impact depending on the intentions and motivations of those using it. The foremost priority, he stressed, should be to retain human judgement and control at all stages of technological design, development and integration.

He called for appropriate safeguards, regulations and governance frameworks to ensure that technological advances served peace rather than becoming instruments of geopolitical dominance and war.

In the military domain, he advocated restraint and confidence-building measures to reduce the risks of miscalculation and compressed decision-making, particularly in the nuclear domain.

The Pakistani envoy also warned against allowing advanced technologies to become the monopoly of a few powerful countries, arguing that all member states, including developing countries, should participate in their democratic, inclusive and equitable development.

He said measures introduced in the name of technological safety should not become instruments for denying other countries access to technology and infrastructure. All member states, particularly developing countries, retained their inalienable right to the peaceful use of technology, he added.

Shah also highlighted the growing dangers of misinformation, disinformation, fake news and cyberattacks, including attacks on critical infrastructure by state and non-state actors.

“The UN Charter and international law apply in all situations, irrespective of underlying technologies,” he said, calling for collective efforts to clarify the application of international law and take concrete action against emerging threats.

He advocated practical confidence-building measures, including crisis communication, deconfliction and mutual restraint, to reduce mistrust, prevent accidental escalation and manage risks associated with military and foundational technologies.

The ambassador said the fragmented and dispersed nature of emerging technologies required layered governance frameworks, accountability measures and, where appropriate, legally binding instruments.

“Delaying regulation to secure advantage and domination will not work,” he cautioned, adding that discriminatory agendas and forums with selective representation would not help address the challenges.

Pakistan believes discussions on the development and deployment of emerging technologies, particularly their implications for arms control, should take place in inclusive and representative multilateral forums under UN auspices.

While supporting the Security Council’s engagement with emerging technologies, Shah said its discussions should focus on their operational implications, including the implementation of Council mandates in peacekeeping, peacebuilding and conflict resolution.

He also highlighted the potential of artificial intelligence and unmanned aerial vehicles to improve civilian protection and the safety and security of UN peacekeepers.

The country’s envoy added that the use of new technologies, particularly UAVs and AI, by terrorist groups and other non-state actors could also be addressed in the renewal of Security Council mandates.

articles.title: Thieves steal 49,000 litres of fuel from PSO pipeline in Islamabad
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Thieves have stolen 49,000 litres of fuel worth Rs17.6 million from the main Pakistan State Oil (PSO) pipeline laid in the capital’s rural area since October 16.

Following a complaint lodged by Mohammad Rahmet Ullah, an official at the PSO Sihala Terminal, police registered a case under Sections 462-B (tampering with petroleum pipelines) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

According to the FIR, the PSO Sihala installations are connected to Attock Refinery Limited via a 15-kilometre-long, eight-inch-diameter pipeline. Since October 16, officials have noticed a continuous drop in pipeline pressure during specific hours each day, prompting strict surveillance of the line to track down the oil theft.

PSO security guards, while patrolling the pipeline, observed suspicious activity involving a Shahzore truck equipped with a tank at a house in Model Town on Nov 23. The matter was brought to the knowledge of the area police.

Later, the police, accompanied by a PSO security team, reached the house and found a man there.

The house was searched, leading to the discovery of a truck, a Bolan vehicle and a motorcycle. Upon further inquiry and based on information provided by the man, a pit was discovered beneath a floor slab in the house’s kitchen.

A high-pressure pipe and a nozzle were found installed in the pit for the purpose of stealing oil. The man further revealed that the pipeline runs along the wall, extending towards a plot.

Acting on the information, the floor of the sitting room was dug, revealing a tunnel underneath. According to the man, it connected directly to the main pipeline of the PSO.

During investigation, the man revealed that in collusion with his accomplices, he had long been involved in stealing petroleum products from various locations and at different times.

The complainant said the accused caused a loss of approximately 49,000 litres of diesel worth Rs17.6 million to PSO.

In October 2024, thieves stole 302,046 litres of diesel worth over Rs80 million from a PSO pipeline laid in the area of Humak in a similar way.

In July 2026, the Federal Investigation Agency, in a joint operation with PSO, busted a network involved in stealing diesel from PSO’s main pipeline near Sihala and arrested two suspects.

The network reportedly operated for five to six months, and 20,000 litres of diesel were being illegally extracted from the pipeline daily.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: Imran asks PTI to reach out to Fazl, other parties
articles.summary:
• Core committee briefed on jailed founder’s instructions to expand political alliance
• PPP urges PTI to first prove its role as effective opposition before seeking wider cooperation

ISLAMABAD: The PTI’s core committee was informed that incarcerated party founder Imran Khan wanted it to expand its political alliance and reach out to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties to build a broader front.

Meanwhile, the PPP played down the PTI’s invitation to join a new alliance, urging the latter to first demonstrate its role as the main opposition party inside and outside parliament.

The instructions were conveyed to the core committee during an overnight meeting that began on Monday. Lawyer Latif Khosa briefed members on his meeting with Mr Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, at Adiala jail on Nov 11. Another of Mr Khan’s lawyers, Salman Safdar, was also present during the meeting with the couple.

In a statement issued on Tuesday after the core committee meeting, the PTI said Mr Khan had expressed “complete confidence” in the opposition leadership and directed the party to expand its political alliance.

New provinces

Mr Khosa also briefed the core committee, chaired by PTI Chairman Barris­ter Gohar Ali Khan, on Mr Khan’s inst­r­uctions regarding the creation of new provinces.

The committee was told that Mr Khan wanted the matter to be “deliberated up­­on in detail at the forthcoming meeting of PTI’s parliamentary party”. Recom­me­ndations would subsequently be prese­n­ted to him for a decision, the statement said.

The committee expressed serious concern over Mr Khan’s health and demanded implementation of the Supreme Court’s Aug 18 order directing authorities to transfer him to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad.

It also called for the implementation of judicial orders concerning Bushra Bibi’s medical treatment.

Referring to a recent letter written by Mr Khan to top judges, the committee urged the judiciary to take immediate notice of his concerns and ensure access to personal physicians for a comprehensive medical examination and treatment.

The core committee condemned the continued detention of Sohail Afridi, who has been rendered non-functional as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister following the imposition of governor’s rule, and other PTI lawmakers.

It criticised the extension of detention orders under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) against elected representatives and political workers.

The committee appealed to the Federal Constitutional Court and its chief justice to modify the existing stay order concerning Section 3 of the MPO and provide relief to political leaders and workers who had been granted bail by the Peshawar High Court before Nov 5 but whose release orders remained unimplemented because of the stay.

It also decided to observe Nov 26 as “Martyrs’ Day” to commemorate those killed during the 2024 protests.

‘Opposition’s role’

Meanwhile, PPP General Secretary Nayyer Hussain Bukhari said the party had not decided to withdraw from the federal government, although the possibility could be considered at a meeting of its Central Executive Committee in light of prevailing circumstances.

He said President Asif Ali Zardari had always prioritised political reconciliation and consensus, but the PPP was also paying a “political price” for being part of the government.

Mr Bukhari said the PTI had yet to respond to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s invitation to return to parliamentary standing committees. He said the PTI was neither visible as an effective opposition in parliament nor outside it and should present a clear political agenda instead of merely raising slogans.

On the issue of new provinces, he said the PPP wanted both the PML-N and the PTI to clearly announce their positions. He questioned the silence of PML-N President Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, saying statements by PML-N ministers also reflected confusion and inconsistency.

He noted that the PTI also maintained that the creation of new provinces was part of its manifesto.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: Pakistan eyes $1.21 billion disbursement next month
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Exe­cutive Board of the Intern­a­tional Monetary Fund (IMF) is expected to appr­ove on Dec 11 the disbursement of about $1.21 billion to Pakistan under two concurrent program­mes — the $7bn Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the $1.4bn Resilience and Sus­t­ainability Facility (RSF).

The approval would mark the completion of the fourth review under the EFF and the third under the RSF.

Upon approval, Pakis­tan will have access to about $1bn (760 million Special Drawing Rights, or SDRs) under the EFF and about $210m (154m SDRs) under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to about $5.7bn.

The two sides had reac­hed a staff-level agr­eem­ent (SLA) in the first week of October. Both programmes — the 37-month EFF and the 28-month RSF — are scheduled to conclude by September 2027.

The IMF staff had acknowledged in the SLA that programme implementation under the EFF rema­ined broadly on track despite a challenging external environment.

It also noted Pakistan’s strong commitment to preserving macroeconomic stability, strengthening public finances, keeping inflation within the State Bank of Pakistan’s target range on a sustained basis, enhancing energy sector viability and strengthening social protection.

The IMF team, led by Iva Petrova, had also completed the 2026 Article IV consultation, a regular assessment of the country’s economic performance and policies, alongside the fourth review under the EFF and the third under the RSF during discussions held from Sept 23 to Oct 7.

The IMF staff had noted that, supported by the EFF, the authorities had successfully navigated the impact of the Middle East conflict and strong policies helped preserve macroeconomic stability.

Real GDP growth reached four per cent in the first three quarters of FY26. Although higher energy prices and supply disruptions subsequently weakened growth momentum somewhat, the IMF estimated full-year growth at 3.6pc.

The Fund had also noted that the current account remained broadly balanced in FY26, supported by strong remittances, while gross foreign exchange reserves rose to about $21.5bn by end-September.

Sovereign credit rating upgrades and renewed access to international financial markets also pointed to stronger policy credibility.

Nevertheless, the Fund highlighted considerable risks, particularly those arising from geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, tighter global financial conditions and trade disruptions.

The two sides had agreed that maintaining sound macroeconomic policies was critical to safeguarding stability amid continued vulnerability to external shocks.

In this regard, policy priorities would continue to include maintaining fiscal discipline through steadfast implementation of the FY27 budget, anchored by an underlying primary surplus of 2pc of GDP and supported by tax policy and revenue administration measures to place public debt on a sustainable downward trajectory.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: Achakzai proposes national govt, comprehensive reforms
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Tehreek Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) head and Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai on Tuesday called for the formation of a national government and comprehensive constitutional and political reforms to steer the country out of the mounting crises it was facing.

Addressing a multi-party conference at the Javed Iqbal Auditorium of the Lahore High Court Bar Association (LHCBA), he said decisions having national importance should be made through consultations among elected representatives and all democratic political forces, instead of being left to a handful of individuals.

He stressed the need for constitutional supremacy, parliamentary sovereignty and “restoration of democracy”, saying Lahore and its bar associations had historically played a significant role in the struggle for constitutional rule.

Expressing concern over the deteriorating law and order situation, Achakzai said unrest and bloodshed continuing in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan had now spread to Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as well.

Says new setup comprising institutions, parties should ‘provide military dignified exit from politics’

Deploring daily casualties in the troubled areas, he said protecting citizens’ life and property should be the foremost responsibility of the state institutions and political leadership.

Referring to PTI founder Imran Khan, Achakzai said the people had given him a majority mandate which was subsequently taken away.

He expressed concern over Imran’s political circumstances and health, alleging that attempts are being made to break his resolve and isolate him. He said that he and Senate opposition leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas would not allow such attempts to succeed.

Proposing a national government, comprising major state institutions, political parties and other stakeholders, he said the new setup should address the past injustices, introduce constitutional reforms and provide the military a “constitutional and dignified exit from politics”.

He also condemned the alleged detention of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in Lahore and the denial of permission to attend the conference.

Speaking on the occasion, Allama Abbas said the country needed to return to constitutional rule and respect the people’s mandate, adding that freedom and fundamental rights were divine and nobody had the authority to take them away.

He questioned whether jailed PTI leaders Dr Yasmin Rashid, Umar Sarfraz Cheema, Ejaz Chaudhry and Aleema Khan were terrorists. He also asked about the whereabouts of the suspended KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and provincial assembly speaker.

Questioning the federal government’s approach towards the provinces, Abbas asked whether it intended to decide unilaterally how the federating units should remain part of the federation.

He said the existing system had failed as it offered nothing to the poor.

Former president of the Supreme Court Bar Association, Hamid Khan, and other bar leaders also addressed the conference.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: Court allows plea for messaging-app records of Mir Raza, two others
articles.summary:
KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday allowed an application filed by the investigating officer of the Mir Ali Raza murder case seeking records from multiple messaging and social media apps belonging to the deceased, his business partner Ahmed Bharday and another person.

At the outset of the hearing, Mr Bharday and Ali Shaz appeared in court in response to a notice issued on an application filed by the IO, DSP Fareed Ahmed Khan.

In the application, the IO stated that it had become necessary to obtain relevant digital information of their WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, iMessage, LinkedIn and FaceTime accounts to ascertain their digital communications and activities before the incident.

The IO stated that the digital records were important to establish the sequence of events, identify those who remained in contact with the deceased, trace possible leads and collect corroborative electronic evidence relevant to the investigation.

He added that he had initially approached the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency, but it informed him that his request could not be entertained without directions from the court.

The court asked Mr Bharday and Mr Shaz whether they had any objection to the application, and both replied in the negative.

The court allowed the application and also granted 14 more days to the IO for submission of the final charge sheet.

Mir Raza went missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS. His body, bearing a gunshot wound, was found in the bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar a day later.

A case was registered at the Ferozabad police station under Sections 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine person), 302 (premeditated murder) and 201 (causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

More than three months have passed, but investigators have failed to identify the actual culprit in Mir Raza’s alleged murder or establish the circumstances surrounding the discovery of his body.

A joint investigation team formed on the recommendation of a judicial commission is currently investigating the case.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: UK police arrest two men after break-in at William’s home
articles.summary:
LONDON: Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said on Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the countryside retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine, who were not in residence at the time.

Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, eastern England, after the local force received a call just before 6pm on Monday of “suspicious activity”, Norfolk police said in a statement. Anmer Hall where William, Kate and their three children occasionally live — especially during the school holidays — was broken into, according to UK media. The 10-bedroom red-brick Georgian manor was gifted to the couple by the late Queen Elizabeth II after their marriage.

The men “were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass”, police said. The sprawling Sandringham estate is owned by William’s father King Charles. Police said the property “was unoccupied” at the time and the men remained in custody.

William and Kate mainly live at their home on the Windsor estate, just west of London. Kensington Palace, which handles the affairs of William, the heir to the throne, did not immediately reply to a request for comment. Charles’s disgraced brother, the former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, moved to Sandringham earlier this year and lives about a mile from Anmer Hall. The king ousted Andrew from his home of two decades in Windsor and stripped him of his royal titles amid the fallout from his brother’s alleged dealings with the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: $150m Punjab education project downgraded
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The World Bank has slightly downgraded a $150 million education project in Punjab, apparently due to the non-mobilisation of technical assistance and the unavailability of baseline data, despite substantial progress against other targets.

In its public disclosure, the Washington-based multilateral downgraded the overall implementation progress from ‘satisfactory’ to ‘moderately satisfactory’. It kept unchanged the progress towards development of projects’ development objectives at ‘moderately satisfactory’. The overall risk rating was also kept unchanged at moderate.

“The project has continued to make progress against its targets, including achievement of the financial targets for the previous fiscal year. Progress has been recorded across the performance-based conditions,” the bank said.

Enrolment in public-private partnership schools has increased substantially from the project baseline, with the year-four target achieved ahead of schedule. In addition, 1,092 more schools now provide early childhood care and education that meets quality standards.

World Bank cites missing technical help and baseline data despite enrolment gains

On the other hand, classroom construction has yet to begin, although preparatory activities have progressed. “The formal restructuring of the project to reflect the government’s revised construction plan remains an important next step,” the bank said, adding that the technical assistance supporting several reform deliverables has not yet been mobilised.

Baseline data for the project also re­­mains unavailable and will be ad­­dressed during restructuring. “Continued progr­ess on these arrangements, alongside the commencement of classroom construction, will be important to sustain implementation and achieve the project’s intended results,” the bank warned.

The World Bank’s executive directors approved the $150m loan in June 2024, with a closing deadline of June 2029. The loan aims to increase participation rates of girls and boys in pre-primary and primary grades and to enhance reading proficiency in primary grades in Punjab.

The project “Getting Results: Access and Delivery of Quality Education Services in Punjab Project (GRADES)” was designed to improve learning outcomes, recover from learning losses during the Covid-19 pandemic, strengthen school management, and expand school participation.

This should contribute to higher completion rates and more years of schooling, with improved learning for both girls and boys. The project is expected to directly benefit approximately five million children, 7,000 headteachers, 165,000 teachers, and more than 3,000 teacher mentors in public schools and Punjab Education Foundation schools.

Project documents reported that, as of June 2024, more than seven million children in Punjab were out of school. The GRADES project was expected to help the Government of Punjab substantially reduce this number.

In parallel, the project aimed to imp­rove foundational learning outcomes for boys and girls already in school. It plan­ned to do so by scaling up and strengthening public-private partnerships, improving school readiness among young children, enhancing the quality and use of teaching and learning materials and assessments, and improving the learning environment in schools.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: Five women killed each hour by relatives in 2025: UN
articles.summary:
UNITED NATIONS: More than 47,000 women and girls, or around five per hour, were killed by relatives around the world in 2025, a figure broadly unchanged from previous years, according to a UN report published on Tuesday.

The number of women and girls killed by an intimate partner or a family member has fluctuated between 45,000 and 51,000 over the past several years, according to estimates by UN Women and the UN Office on Drugs and Crime.

Of the 78,000 women and girls who were victims of intentional homicide last year, around 60 per cent were killed by an intimate partner or family member, the report said ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

The estimated 47,000 victims represent 129 women and girls killed every day. The figure was calculated using an analysis of statistics from 122 countries and territories.

While women accounted for 19pc of homicide victims worldwide in 2025, 60pc of them were killed in the private sphere. By contrast, 11pc of male homicide victims were killed in such circumstances.

The UN stressed the “urgency of ensuring that the prevention of domestic violence addresses intimate relationships, as well as relationships in wider family structures”. No region was completely safe but Africa once again recorded the highest number of women and girls killed by intimate partners or family members, at 22,100.

Asia followed with 15,100 victims, ahead of the Americas with 7,400, Europe with 2,100 and Oceania with 300.

The report also noted that while homicide rates have fallen globally, rates of femicide have declined more slowly, particularly in the Americas and Europe.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: India stops ‘cockroach’ drive leader from flying to London
articles.summary:
NEW DELHI: A leader of India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement has said he was prevented from leaving New Delhi to fly to Britain to deliver talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May.

Das, who was due to fly out early Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.

The incident comes a month after he was detained for defying a security crackdown in New Delhi during protests demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner.

“This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE (London School of Economics), Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement,” Das said in a social media post late Monday.

“Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!”

Das was due to speak at the prestigious Oxford Uni­on society on Dec 1.

articles.title: Pakistan warns of global energy crisis as conflicts disrupt supplies
articles.summary:
WASHINGTON: Pakistan has warned that the spread of conflicts is threatening global energy and food supplies, disrupting supply chains and driving up prices, with particularly severe consequences for developing countries.

Speaking at a UN Security Council briefing on Monday, Pakistan’s Permanent Representative, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, called for protecting critical energy infrastructure, maritime routes and global food supply chains, stressing that the growing number of conflicts was creating humanitarian and economic challenges far beyond the areas directly affected.

“There is little doubt that our world is facing a rapidly shifting and, as a corollary, an unstable geo-political situation,” he told the council.

He said conflicts across different regions were putting tremendous strain on global food and energy supplies, fracturing supply chains, restricting access to essential commodities and sending prices soaring.

Islamabad reaffirms support for peaceful resolution of disputes

“The resulting humanitarian consequences have been devastating, impacting lives and livelihoods of peoples not only in the areas directly affected by these conflicts, but far beyond the confines of the conflict zones, especially the developing countries,” he said.

Pakistan is particularly vulnerable to disruptions in Middle Eastern energy supplies because of its heavy dependence on imported oil and gas. According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the country is a net oil and gas importer, with 81 per cent of its fuel imports originating in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. The Fund has warned that higher international energy prices and regional price premiums are worsening Pakistan’s economic outlook, putting pressure on its current account and threatening to push up inflation.

The impact has also been felt in the petroleum and power sectors. Disruptions to Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies following the outbreak of the Middle East war prompted Pakistan to consider expensive spot-market purchases and alternative fuel arrangements.

In April, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik told Reuters that spot LNG cargoes were trading at between $20 and $30 per million British thermal units (mmBtu). The State Bank of Pakistan subsequently reported that inflation accelerated sharply from March 2026 onwards, averaging 10.2 per cent during March-June, driven partly by higher global energy and commodity prices following the Middle East conflict.

The briefing, chaired by Latvian President Edgars Rinkvis, focused on protecting critical energy infrastructure and Black Sea lifelines of global food supplies. It was held under the Security Council agenda item on the maintenance of peace and security of Ukraine.

Shah expressed deep concern over the escalation of hostilities, loss of human life and attacks on civilian infrastructure, including energy facilities, transportation networks and commercial vessels, both within conflict zones and beyond.

Reaffirming Pakistan’s position on the primacy of international law and international humanitarian law, he said the protection of civilians and critical food and energy infrastructure must be ensured in all conflicts.

He urged all parties to facilitate “rapid and unimpeded humanitarian assistance”, in accordance with international humanitarian law, and called for stronger international cooperation to safeguard global food and energy supply chains.

The ambassador highlighted the close links between energy supplies, fertilisers, maritime transportation and agricultural trade, warning that disruptions in these interconnected sectors could spread food insecurity well beyond conflict-affected regions.

Recent conflicts, he said, had demonstrated how interruptions to energy supplies and maritime transportation could have far-reaching consequences for food security and vulnerable economies.

Emphasising that the protection of essential infrastructure alone could not provide a lasting solution, Shah called for resolving conflicts through peaceful means.

“There can be no lasting food security without peace. There can be no substitute for the actual resolution of conflicts, through peaceful means, in accordance with the UN Charter and international law,” he stressed.

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for efforts aimed at achieving enduring and peaceful resolutions to conflicts and mitigating the adverse global consequences of disruptions to food and energy supplies.

The briefing was also addressed by UN Under-Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo, World Food Programme Executive Director Luke Lindberg and UN Development Programme Administrator Alexander De Croo.

Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

articles.title: Govt reduces diesel price by Rs4 per litre, petrol by Re1 per litre
articles.summary:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre and that of diesel by Rs4 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs318 per litre and diesel at Rs353 per litre on Nov 25 (Wednesday).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

articles.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri to unveil SS27 collection in Abuja
articles.summary:
Nigerian fashion designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri will unveil her Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, tagged Reverie, in Abuja later this month, extending the presentation of her latest designs beyond Lagos to the Federal Capital Territory.

The Abuja showcase follows the collection’s unveiling at The Citadel, in Lagos, during the Lagos Fashion Week period. The presentation is expected to bring together fashion industry stakeholders, luxury consumers, government officials and other guests in the capital.

The move also comes as the fashion house seeks to strengthen its presence in Northern Nigeria, building on its existing Abuja flagship. The showcase provides an opportunity for the brand to reach more consumers in the region and expand its engagement with Nigeria’s luxury fashion market.

The Reverie collection explores themes of renewal, playfulness and reinvention, drawing inspiration from nature and the experience of walking through a forest. Its designs combine sculptural tailoring with more fluid pieces intended for everyday retail.

The collection features materials such as sheer organza, Chantilly lace, chiffon and hand-woven aso-oke, alongside nature-inspired embroidery. It also incorporates contemporary interpretations of traditional Nigerian clothing, including the iro, buba and danshiki, as well as eveningwear and menswear. The designs feature a range of colours, moving from neutral shades to lime green, fuchsia, pink and deep burgundy.

The Abuja presentation is part of activities marking 16 years of the fashion house’s operations. The Lagos unveiling was accompanied by the third edition of its industry symposium, Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held at the British Council in Ikoyi.

The symposium brought together participants to discuss the fashion industry’s development and the role of industry practitioners in building a lasting fashion business.

The Abuja event will feature a runway presentation and private viewing of the SS27 collection. The fashion house said the event would bring together diplomats, government representatives, fashion editors and luxury consumers.

The post Ejiro Amos Tafiri to unveil SS27 collection in Abuja appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: 2027: Morka questions Obi, NDC over ‘Rig and die’ slogan
articles.summary:
The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, Felix Morka, has questioned the meaning and legal basis of the Nigeria Democratic Congress’ (NDC) ‘rig and die’ slogan, asking when election rigging became an offence punishable by death under Nigerian law.

Morka argued that anyone suspected of manipulating an election should be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law rather than face punishment determined by a political party or its supporters.

He made the remarks during an appearance on News Central on Wednesday while reacting to allegations of political violence involving supporters of the NDC and the APC.

His comments followed an explanation by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who had defended the slogan during an interview with Channels Television after a town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday.

Obi had clarified that the message was directed at preventing electoral malpractice, not discouraging political campaigns.

“They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” Obi said.

However, Morka questioned the implication of the slogan, particularly the suggestion that people accused of rigging elections should die.

“So, if somebody rigs an election, since when did Nigerian law prescribe the death penalty for rigging an election?” he asked.

The APC spokesman maintained that allegations of electoral offences should be handled through the established legal process.

He also accused the NDC of making unsubstantiated claims that the APC was responsible for political violence, arguing that the party had not reported the alleged incidents to the police or sought independent investigations.

Morka further alleged that some NDC supporters had displayed machetes at political gatherings, referring to videos he said were circulating online from Lagos and Delta states.

He questioned why the NDC had not denied the videos, although the allegations and his interpretation of the footage were his own claims.

The post 2027: Morka questions Obi, NDC over ‘Rig and die’ slogan appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: CAF announces finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year Award
articles.summary:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi and Senegalese forward Sadio Mané among the nominees.

The shortlist was drawn from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for their respective clubs and national teams during the assessment period.

Morocco has three representatives among the finalists, while Senegal accounts for two, highlighting the countries’ strong showing during the period under review.

Hakimi, who features for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the individual honour after playing a key role in the club’s UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 triumphs.

The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON.

The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph.

Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals.

Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI.

Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals.

The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos.

The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time.

The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition.

Full list of 2026 Men’s Player of the Year finalists

Achraf Hakimi (Morocco)

Sadio Mané (Senegal)

Brahim Diaz (Morocco)

Pape Gueye (Senegal)

Ismael Saibari (Morocco)

articles.title: I never tapped Ribadu’s phone – El-Rufai
articles.summary:
Former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has told a Federal High Court in Abuja that his claim about listening to the telephone conversation of National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, was an exaggeration made during a political exchange.

El-Rufai gave the explanation while testifying in his ongoing phone-tapping case, insisting that he neither intercepted Ribadu’s calls nor possessed the equipment or technical expertise to do so.

Under questioning by his lawyer, Paul Erokoro, during Tuesday’s court session, the former governor said he never owned call interception equipment.

He also told the court that he lacked the technical knowledge to conduct telephone surveillance and had no access to Ribadu’s communication systems.

Explaining his choice of words during a February interview on Arise Television, El-Rufai said his use of “we” referred to opposition politicians and was not an admission of personal involvement in phone interception.

“I used ‘we’ to refer to opposition politicians. When I said ‘tapped’, it was an embellishment intended to make the government feel the pain we are feeling. It was rhetorical and exaggerated. My objective was to engage in political retort and linguistic flourish,” he said.

The former governor’s clarification came as he continued his testimony in the phone-tapping case before the Federal High Court in Abuja.

articles.title: Tinubu’s anti-violence directive put into action in Kogi, says APC Chieftain
articles.summary:
A chieftain of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Alhaji Mohammed Usman, has denied that the party had any involvement in reported campaign violence in Delta, Sokoto and Kebbi states.

Usman said the incidents should not be blamed on the APC, arguing that local political disputes and the actions of individual actors were responsible. He added that the APC in Kogi State was guided by the same principles as the party elsewhere.

In a statement, the chieftain said the peaceful rally held in Kogi State by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and his party offered evidence of the APC’s commitment to peaceful politics.

“Atiku can now testify to what happened in Kogi State, where he and his party held a peaceful rally,” Usman said. He praised Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo for ensuring the event proceeded peacefully, adding that the governor’s actions reflected President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s message of peace and unity.

Usman said Atiku should acknowledge the peaceful conduct of the rally and recognise the President’s efforts to promote unity. He added that President Tinubu had warned politicians and their supporters against violence ahead of the 2027 general elections and had pledged firm action against political thuggery and other anti-democratic activities.

According to Usman, the President has also directed security agencies to maintain public order and confront anyone seeking to disrupt it.

In a statement titled, “Let’s Shun Violence: Our Campaigns Must Be About Issues That Promote the Welfare of Our People,” Usman described the peaceful Kogi rally as a setback for what he called opposition propaganda and “name-calling and blame games.”

He also attributed the reported violence in Delta State to internal political disputes, citing a court ruling concerning the state’s Delta Central Senatorial District. Usman said the court ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to delist former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, following a case instituted by Professor Alexander Akpodiete.

Usman further said the court found that the NDC had failed to submit its membership register to INEC 21 days before its primary and that Omo-Agege was not listed in the register. He also cited the court’s finding that Omo-Agege had participated in an APC primary on May 18, 2026. Usman argued that the dispute reflected internal party grievances rather than APC involvement.

He urged Atiku and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to tell Nigerians that the Kogi rally was peaceful, crediting Governor Ododo’s conduct and the implementation of President Tinubu’s directive.

We are aware that some bad elements were hoping for violence so they could blame Mr. President. However, we thank God for Governor Usman Ododo, who—as the Chief Security Officer of the state—ensured that the President’s directive was implemented to the letter,” the APC chieftain said.

“Atiku came to Kogi State for a campaign, and our party did what was necessary to ensure peace,” Usman said. “The President’s directive was not just words; it was put into action.”

The post Tinubu’s anti-violence directive put into action in Kogi, says APC Chieftain appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Murray-Bruce says Nigeria not dumping ground, demands five-year accountability for car, solar dealers
articles.summary:
Former Bayelsa East senator, Ben Murray-Bruce has called on the Federal Government to stop Nigeria from becoming a dumping ground for substandard vehicles, solar systems and other consumer products sold without warranty, spare parts or after-sales service.

In a post on X on Wednesday, Murray-Bruce said Nigeria has become the world’s favourite dumping ground, and Nigerians are paying for it with their hard-earned money.

“Let me say this plainly: Nigeria has become the world’s favourite dumping ground, and we are paying for it with our hard-earned money,” he wrote.

He said every month, new car brands, many of them Chinese, open showrooms in Lagos and Abuja, sell vehicles with no real warranty, no spare parts and no after-sales service, and then close shop and vanish, leaving buyers stranded with vehicles nobody can repair.

Murray-Bruce cited his personal experience with a solar system installed in his home, saying the company went bankrupt and left Nigeria within a year, leaving the investment wasted because there is no one to service it.

“I know this pain. I invested in a solar system for my home. Within a year, the company that installed it went bankrupt and left Nigeria,” he said.

“Millions of Nigerians are buying inverters, batteries, and panels with the same broken promise: no warranty, no support, and no one to hold accountable when things fail.”

He described the practice as exploitation rather than trade, arguing that in serious countries, a company cannot sell a car or a power system and simply disappear, but must prove its capacity, keep spare parts, and stand behind its products for years.

“This is not trade; it is exploitation. In serious countries, a company cannot sell a car or a power system and simply disappear,” he said. “Why should Nigerians deserve anything less?”

Murray-Bruce called on the Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, and the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan Enoh, to set the rules for who enters the Nigerian market.

He also urged the National Automotive Design and Development Council under Otunba Oluwemimo Osanipin to license only dealerships with real capacity, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria under Dr. Ifeanyi Okeke to stop substandard products at the borders, and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission under Tunji Bello to protect buyers.

On solar and inverters, he called on the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to insist on certified installers with lasting service obligations.

He proposed that any dealership that sells to Nigerians and shuts down within less than five years must be held accountable, with its directors pursued and its customers compensated.

“Every company must post a bond, guarantee spare parts and service for a minimum number of years, and register a local service centre before it sells a single product. Only reputable companies with a track record should be allowed in,” he said.

He stressed, “Nigeria is a market of more than 200 million people. We are not a dumping ground, and it is time we started acting like it.”

The post Murray-Bruce says Nigeria not dumping ground, demands five-year accountability for car, solar dealers appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: LASG includes ‘Lagos to London’ in SS1–SS3 literature curriculum
articles.summary:
By Chukwuma Umeorah

The Lagos State Government has included Lagos to London, a novel by Nigerian author Lola Aworanti-Ekugo, in the Literature-in-English curriculum for senior secondary school students, covering Senior Secondary School 1 to 3 (SS1–SS3).

The inclusion places the contemporary Nigerian novel among literary texts to be studied by students in public and private senior secondary schools across the state, providing an opportunity for young learners to engage with themes of migration, identity, ambition, societal expectations and the choices confronting Nigerians seeking opportunities abroad.

Published by Aworanti-Ekugo, Lagos to London “follows the experiences of two young Nigerians, Remi Coker and Nnamdi Okonkwo, who leave the country for the United Kingdom in search of better opportunities but approach migration from different backgrounds and perspectives. While Remi, who comes from the prominent Coker family, travels to London to pursue a law degree with the expectation of returning to Nigeria to eventually take over her family’s law firm, Nnamdi is driven by frustration with persistent strikes in federal universities and his determination to relocate permanently.”

The novel’s inclusion in the state curriculum brings the subject of migration, popularly described as ‘japa’ in Nigeria, into the classroom, offering students an opportunity to examine the motivations behind emigration, the expectations of life abroad and questions surrounding national development and the responsibilities of young Nigerians.

Commenting on the development, Aworanti-Ekugo said, “I wrote Lagos to London with the hope of telling real and relevant stories that resonate with young Africans today, encouraging them to think more deeply about identity, ambition, choices, opportunity and the world around them. Seeing the novel included in the Lagos State curriculum for senior secondary schools is particularly meaningful because it allows these important conversations to reach a wider audience of young people, inspiring them to broaden their horizons and engage with different perspectives through literature.”

The adoption also provides an avenue for students to study contemporary African fiction alongside the themes and literary techniques examined in their Literature-in-English lessons, while engaging with issues that reflect experiences within Nigerian society.

Beyond migration, the novel examines the influence of family expectations, educational challenges and individual aspirations on young people’s decisions, particularly as they navigate opportunities in an increasingly interconnected world.

articles.title: HIV prevention: NACA, ASWHAN, CHAI seek stronger community involvement, wider access to new drugs
articles.summary:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

The National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA), the Association of Women Living with HIV and AIDS in Nigeria (ASWHAN) and the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) have called for stronger community participation, sustainable funding and wider access to innovative prevention tools to accelerate Nigeria’s efforts to end HIV as a public health threat by 2030.

They made the call at the 2026 Nigeria HIV Prevention Conference, in Abuja, on Tuesday, where stakeholders stressed the need to move beyond existing interventions and adopt sustainable, inclusive and community-centred strategies to prevent new infections.

Speaking at the conference, NACA Director-General, Dr. Temitope Ilori, said Nigeria had recorded commendable progress in expanding access to HIV testing and treatment, improving the quality of life of people living with HIV and saving lives.

However, she warned that treatment gains alone would not be sufficient to end the epidemic, insisting that prevention must remain at the centre of the country’s HIV response.

Ilori, whose address was themed, “Building to Last: Re-imagining HIV Prevention Strategies in Nigeria”, said the country must rethink existing approaches and develop prevention systems capable of surviving individual projects, funding cycles and changing global priorities.

She identified domestic resource mobilisation, stronger national and state ownership, integration of prevention services into existing health systems and sustained community engagement as critical to achieving the 2030 target.

The NACA boss said the conference’s 19 sessions would focus on five priority areas, including protecting young people, expanding prevention choices, strengthening sustainable systems, promoting community leadership and using research and evidence to improve outcomes.

She urged participants to ensure that their deliberations produced practical strategies, stronger partnerships and measurable commitments.

Also speaking, National Coordinator of ASWHAN, Mrs Esther Hindi, called for greater involvement of women living with HIV, young people, key populations and community-based organisations in developing policies and programmes.

Hindi said women living with HIV should not be regarded merely as beneficiaries of interventions but as important partners with the experience and expertise to shape effective prevention strategies.

She advocated improved access to HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), condoms, treatment and sexual and reproductive health services.

She also urged the government to accelerate efforts towards eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, insisting that no child should be born with the virus when preventive interventions were available.

According to her, every pregnant woman deserves timely, uninterrupted and quality healthcare services, irrespective of her circumstances.

Hindi further called for stronger action against stigma and discrimination, which she said continued to discourage people from accessing essential health services.

In its goodwill message, the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) commended the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and NACA for providing a platform for stakeholders to assess progress, identify implementation gaps and strengthen partnerships.

The organisation highlighted emerging innovations, particularly injectable cabotegravir and lenacapavir, describing them as important opportunities to expand prevention choices, improve access and reach more people with effective HIV prevention services.

CHAI reaffirmed its commitment to working with governments at federal and state levels and other partners to promote equitable access to HIV prevention services.

It also acknowledged the support of Unitaid, the Gates Foundation, Elton John AIDS Foundation and its partnership with ViiV Healthcare in South Africa.

The conference, however, underscored the need for stronger collaboration among government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations, communities and the private sector.

The stakeholders maintained that achieving the 2030 target would require sustained political commitment, predictable financing, innovation and respect for human rights.

They urged participants to translate the conference’s discussions into concrete actions capable of reducing new infections and ensuring that no Nigerian is left behind in HIV prevention efforts.

articles.title: Nigeria, Tanzania seek African action on Women’s health workforce crisis
articles.summary:
By Chukwuma Umeorah

Nigeria and Tanzania are seeking coordinated action across Africa to strengthen the health workforce responsible for delivering healthcare to women, as both countries prepare to host a continental summit aimed at addressing gaps in maternal, reproductive and other women’s health services.

The two countries will convene about 300 decision-makers, including heads of state, health and finance ministers, African Union (AU) officials, development finance institutions and health-sector stakeholders at the inaugural Women’s Health Africa Summit (WHAS 2026), scheduled for December 1 at the State House Banquet Hall, Abuja.

The summit is being anchored by Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, under the leadership of Pate, with presidential facilitation by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Women’s Health.

The summit, themed, “Health Workforce for Better Women’s Health,” is expected to focus on mobilising investment, strengthening healthcare delivery and securing measurable commitments from African countries to improve women’s health across different stages of life.

Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, said the meeting would provide an opportunity for African countries to identify gaps in their healthcare systems, share experiences and take greater responsibility for addressing the continent’s health priorities.

“The Women’s Health Africa Summit is a great platform for bringing together leaders, advocates, practitioners, academics and financiers to identify gaps, mobilise action and facilitate shared learning across countries. Indeed, women’s health is a global issue, and even wealthier countries continue to face significant gaps in this area.

“Ultimately, responsibility lies with us as leaders on the continent. We must take ownership of our health priorities.”

The initiative also seeks to address the capacity of frontline health workers, functional referral systems and community healthcare services, which are considered necessary for reducing preventable maternal and newborn deaths.

Tanzania’s co-hosting role is linked to its leadership of the AU’s maternal and child health agenda under President Samia Suluhu Hassan, who champions the Continental Roadmap on Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) 2026–2030. The roadmap is built around three targets: zero home delivery, zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths, and zero unvaccinated children.

Special Adviser to the Tanzanian President on Maternal and Child Health, Hon. Ummy Ally Mwalimu, said collaboration between the two countries was necessary to translate continental health commitments into measurable results.

“Under the leadership of Her Excellency President Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, AU Champion for Maternal and Child Health, Tanzania is proud to co-host WHAS with Nigeria. Collaboration between our two AU Champions is an implementation imperative, not simply a matter of institutional goodwill. Coordinated leadership is essential to align workforce investment, community health delivery, sustainable financing and accountability with country-led priorities, avoid fragmented efforts and translate continental commitments into measurable results.

“The Three Zeros of the Continental RMNCAH Roadmap depend on competent, adequately supported frontline health workers, functional referral systems and effective community outreach. WHAS, under the theme ‘Health Workforce for Better Women’s Health’, provides a timely platform for these shared commitments.”

Beyond maternal and reproductive healthcare, the summit will address non-communicable diseases, gynaecological conditions and menopause, broadening the focus of women’s healthcare beyond pregnancy and childbirth.

Senior Special Assistant to the President on Women’s Health, Dr. Adanna Steinacker, said the initiative would seek to address the limited attention given to women’s health needs across different stages of life.

“For too long, women’s health has been treated as a secondary concern or viewed narrowly through a single stage of life. WHAS changes that paradigm, bringing African governments, capital, and innovators together to back women’s health across the entire life course as a core pillar of our continent’s social and economic future.”

Financing is also expected to feature prominently, with the organisers identifying innovation, financing and delivery as the three pillars of the summit. The meeting will seek initial commitments from participating countries and institutions, including accelerated action on neglected gynaecological conditions, while establishing a framework for continued African-led cooperation and accountability after the event.

articles.title: Watch: Gaza declares meningitis alert as health ministry blames Israeli restrictions
